tangotango-theme.el is copied unmodified from that commit. It is an Emacs
theme, not a terminal scheme: it carries no 16 ANSI slots. Only four values
are read from it at build time (tools/external-scheme-sources.ts) — the
`default` face's foreground and background, the `cursor` face's background,
and the `region` face's background.

The 16 ANSI slots for the shipped pack come from "Builtin Tango Dark" in
vendor/iterm2-color-schemes (MIT) instead, because TangoTango *is* the Tango
palette: all seven of its accent colours are byte-identical to that scheme's
bright row (#ef2929 #8ae234 #fce94f #729fcf #ad7fa8 #555753 #eeeeec), a
match asserted in test/tools/external-scheme-sources.test.ts so it cannot
drift silently. What makes the pack TangoTango rather than Tango is the four
values above — juba re-grounds the palette on #2e3434 instead of black.

Licence note: Chameleon ships MIT. Only those four bare colour values are
taken from this GPL-3.0 file; see themes/ATTRIBUTION.md.
